products.name: Scoping Application-Permission Mailbox Access — Graph RBAC & Application Access Policies for Exchange Online — Commercial
products.short_description: An app permission like Mail.Read grants your app EVERY mailbox in the tenant — this solution scopes it down to exactly the mailboxes it's allowed to touch, and proves the boundary holds.
products.description:
An app permission like Mail.Read grants your app EVERY mailbox in the tenant — this solution scopes it down to exactly the mailboxes it's allowed to touch, and proves the boundary holds.

Granting an application (or managed identity) an application Graph permission such as Mail.Read is tenant-wide by default: it can read every mailbox in the organization. That is almost never what you want, and it's a finding waiting to happen in a security review. This solution implements least-privilege mailbox access for apps and managed identities — scoping the identity to a specific mailbox or a mail-enabled security group — and validates the boundary. It covers both the established Application Access Policy model and the newer Graph RBAC for Exchange Online approach, when each applies, how to choose, and how to test that in-scope reads succeed while out-of-scope reads are denied.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • The exposure — why an application permission (Mail.Read/Mail.Send/etc.) is tenant-wide, and why that fails a security review
  • Application Access Policy — scope an app/identity to a mail-enabled security group of allowed mailboxes; exact cmdlets flagged verify-with-Microsoft
  • Graph RBAC for Exchange Online — the newer resource-scoped model, when to prefer it over Application Access Policy, and how they differ
  • Choose + apply — a decision path for which model fits, applied to a real app/managed identity scenario with every object named
  • Prove the boundary — validation scripts that confirm in-scope mailbox reads work and out-of-scope reads are denied, with evidence for auditors

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

Application and managed-identity mailbox access scoped to exactly the mailboxes it's allowed to read — least privilege, both scoping models explained, and a tested, auditable boundary.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • MBXRBAC-Discovery.ps1 — inventory apps / managed identities that hold mail-capable APPLICATION
    • MBXRBAC-Report.ps1 — the audit artifact: report every app-permission-to-mailbox scoping (or lack
    • MBXRBAC-Set-AccessPolicy.ps1 — the ONLY state-changer: create/verify the Application Access Policy
    • MBXRBAC-Test-Boundary.ps1 — the boundary proof: authenticate AS THE APPLICATION and confirm the
    • MBXRBAC-Validate.ps1 — PASS/FAIL: confirm a target app/identity is SCOPED (not tenant-wide) to

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
